newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Christmas toy sales up 30 pct -- report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Christmas toy sales up 30 pct -- report.

text.p: Brazilian toy manufacturers are already enjoying a Christmas sales boom, thanks to higher tariffs on imported rivals and economic recovery, the Folha de Sao Paulo newspaper reported on Sunday.
The newspaper said lower imports had already boosted toy firms' turnover by 30 percent compared with 1995, with the quantity of toys being sold rising by 40 percent.
"The greatest impact of the increase in tariffs to 70 percent from 20 percent, announced in July, is being expected for Christmas itself," Folha said.

The newspaper said one of Brazil's main toy manufacturers, Estrela, had already increased sales by up to 15 percent and quoted Estrela president Carlos Tilkian as saying imports had plunged 50 percent on 1995.
Tilkian said Estrela expected to end 1996 with turnover of 120 million reais, up 5.0 percent on 1995.
Brazil's tariff move on toys, harshly criticized by the United States and the European Union, has been highly controversial.

The higher tariff, intended to stem job losses and to give Brazil's domestic toy industry time to restructure, is due to run out at the end of the year, but newspapers report the government may maintain the measure for another three years.
